- When sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for multiple days) and model overreacts with sharp upward spikes, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment turns bearish sharply (e.g., sudden drop >0.67 in sentiment change) and model fails to adjust, lower forecast by 3–8% to match mean reversion trend.
- Model tends to overestimate prices during high news volume periods — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each additional news volume >3.
- When sentiment is flat or mixed (±0.33) and price moves sharply, model often lags — adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged true value.
- If sentiment shows strong negative change (e.g., -0.67+ in sentiment change) and model remains bullish, reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven periods — add 1–3% buffer if sentiment volatility >0.5 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) and model forecasts remain high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- When sentiment is high but news volume is low, model tends to overestimate — reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect muted market reaction.
